items.title: The tired bald rat with a cigarette
items.note: A worn-out hairless rat GIF became everyone's 'I'm done with this conversation' WhatsApp sticker overnight.
items.read: A looping GIF of a weary, hairless rat with smoke curling up has become the internet's favourite argument-ender. X's trend summary says people are copying the post link and pasting it into WhatsApp to turn it into a sticker, and @Franccfc's 'I got you bro, just copy the link' post spread the trick. Others say they'll drop it the second someone says something they don't agree with.

items.title: Bread cat joins the sticker hall of fame
items.note: A cat loafing so perfectly it looks like a bread roll, and Spanish-speaking X wants it on WhatsApp right now.
items.read: Riding the same WhatsApp-sticker wave as the smoking rat, a GIF of a round 'bread cat' peeking out of a crusty loaf shape took off. X's trend summary links it to the classic 'kitty loaf' pose. @kari_ok6 simply posted 'Necesito este sticker en Whatsapp!!' (I need this sticker on WhatsApp) and the replies agreed.

items.title: Peppa Pig hangs up the second Suzy can whistle
items.note: Parents rediscovered the pettiest Peppa Pig scene ever: she teaches her friend to whistle, then hangs up the moment it works.
items.read: A dad watching Peppa Pig with his daughter posted a clip he couldn't believe was real. According to X's trend summary, Peppa can't whistle, calls Suzy Sheep for help, and hangs up the instant Suzy manages it. Parents piled on, with one repost by @ThatboyCano saying one of the funniest things about having kids is getting to see this.

items.title: Sabinus: 'Why is my own always different'
items.note: Nigerian comedian Sabinus dropped a new chaotic skit, and fans say they were laughing in meetings.
items.read: Sabinus posted a new 89-second skit captioned 'Why is my own always different.' X's trend summary describes over-the-top drama, family mishaps and sharp comic timing. Fans shared stories of trying not to laugh at work or wake their families while rewatching it.

items.title: The 'GTA 6 gameplay leak' that looks a lot like Fortnite
items.note: A 'leak' days before launch has fans laughing at its very Fortnite-looking menus. #GTA6 is trending in Saudi too.
items.read: With GTA VI due on 19 November, a 24-second clip labelled 'GTA 6 GAMEPLAY LEAK' went huge. X's trend summary says viewers spotted Fortnite-style menus and map names like 'Lucia Camping B', so the mood is half hype, half doubt. Meanwhile, #GTA6 sits on Saudi Arabia's X trends list this morning, and people are joking about taking launch day off.

items.title: Pattinson as Bond: Cedric Diggory was auditioning for MI6
items.note: Robert Pattinson's James Bond casting set off a meme wave, and this one says he's been practising since Harry Potter.
items.read: Robert Pattinson being named the next James Bond was MemeStand's lead meme of 17 November, with Twilight 'Bond. James Bond.' jokes all over Reddit and X. @pascaliito's take: everyone says Twilight manifested it, but really he did it in Harry Potter by holding his wand like a gun. Conclusion: Cedric Diggory wasn't in the Triwizard Tournament, he was auditioning for MI6.

items.title: 'He wanna pay full price'
items.note: An SNL phone-store line became a chant people are dancing to everywhere.
items.read: A Saturday Night Live sketch with Marcello Hernández as a phone-store worker gave the internet 'papi that is the scenario of the best case' and 'HE WANNA PAY FULL PRICE.' X's trend summary says people are pairing the audio with lip-syncs and group dances in hallways, clubs and shop floors, often to cheer on generous dates. This clip is one of many sharing the bit.

items.title: The goat tower
items.note: Three goats stacked in a wobbly tower, and the internet decided it's about who gets left out of December plans.
items.read: A 10-second clip shows three goats balancing on top of each other in a dusty yard. X's trend summary says viewers are joking about the bottom goat's heavy load and the top one's smug perch. The captions turned it into a warning: 'If dem no involve you, scatter them.'

items.title: Global Ethnosport Cultural Festival, New Murabba
items.note: First edition outside Turkey kicks off in Riyadh tomorrow with 38 traditional sports.
items.read: The Global Ethnosport Cultural Festival comes to Riyadh as part of Riyadh Season 2026, its first edition outside Turkey. Teams and athletes from 18 countries compete in 38 traditional sports and games, from oil, Kazakh and Uzbek wrestling to equestrian sports, archery and folk games.

article.html:
It’s the first edition of the festival outside of Turkey

Riyadh Season 2026 is here, and it’s bringing the whole city to life with something for everyone. The first edition of the Global Ethnosport Cultural Festival outside Turkey will be hosted in Riyadh starting this weekend.

Happening from Thursday November 19 to Saturday November 28 at New Murabba on King Salman bin Abdulaziz Road, the Global Ethnosport Cultural Festival will bring together traditional sporting competitions, global cultures, and interactive experiences.

The event celebrates the sporting and cultural heritage of communities from all over the world. Set to feature teams and athletes from 18 countries across 38 traditional sports and games.

Traditional sports include everything from wrestling and equestrian sports to traditional folk games and mental and strategic games. Wrestling competitions will feature a range of traditional styles, including oil wrestling, Kazakh wrestling, and Uzbek wrestling.

The festival will also feature traditional archery and folk games passed down through generations, as well as equestrian sports, including horseback archery competitions and demonstrations of equestrian skills.

Beyond the sporting action, you can also look forward a cultural village with traditional tents and handicraft workshops, a museum displaying the history of traditional sports, costumes, and heritage artefacts.

You can even get involved in the action yourself with interactive zones where visitors can can try their hands at archery and traditional games, as well as dedicated areas for children and families. On the entertainment front, the festival will also host an international food village, artistic, musical, and folkloric performances on the main stage, and roaming performances too.

Tickets are already on sale and cost SAR15; children under the age of 8 get in for free. Book here.

Dates: Nov 19 to 28

items.title: Riyadh Zoo reopens
items.note: Reopens Thursday for Riyadh Season with giraffe feeding, a crocodile tunnel and live shows.
items.read: Riyadh Zoo opens to visitors on Thursday as part of the seventh Riyadh Season. The 161,000 sqm zoo houses 1,600 animals from more than 170 species, with giraffe feeding, big-cat and bear encounters, a bird house, owl house, crocodile tunnel and kangaroo yard, plus guided tours and kids' activities.

article.html:
Lifestyle

Riyadh Zoo will welcome visitors on Thursday as part of Riyadh Season, offering interactive animal encounters, live shows, and family activities.

Key Takeaways

AI

Riyadh Zoo will open its doors to visitors on Thursday as part of the seventh edition of Riyadh Season, offering a range of interactive experiences, live shows, and family activities that combine entertainment with opportunities to learn about animals and their habitats.

Spanning 161,000 square meters, the zoo is home to 1,600 animals representing more than 170 species. Visitors can explore the diversity of wildlife through experiences such as giraffe feeding, encounters with tigers, lions, and bears, as well as the bird house, owl house, crocodile tunnel, farm area, and kangaroo yard.

The zoo offers more than eight supervised feeding experiences, guided tours introducing visitors to animal behaviors and habitats, and interactive stations designed for families and groups, adding an educational dimension to the visit.

Children's activities include the "Little Farmer" corner for planting, face painting, coloring, and five photo spots featuring animal-inspired models and backgrounds. The zoo also features a variety of food and beverage options, shops, and souvenir kiosks throughout the grounds.

A program of live and entertainment shows will be presented, including circus acts, acrobatic performances, magic shows, and musical bands, along with roaming shows and parades featuring animal-themed characters and costumes.

Riyadh Season, now in its seventh edition, continues to offer a diverse array of entertainment, sports, and arts experiences, bringing together international events, live performances, and family activities that cater to all audiences and reinforce the capital's status as a leading entertainment destination.

items.title: King Abdulaziz Falconry Festival, Malham
items.note: Falconers chase SR36M+ in prizes across 140 rounds, running through Nov 30.
items.read: The King Abdulaziz Falconry Festival began on Tuesday in Malham, north of Riyadh, organized by the National Center for Falcons. Falconers from Saudi Arabia and abroad compete in Milwah (lure flying) and Mazayen (falcon beauty) categories for titles including the King Abdulaziz Cups and Saif Al-Malik.

article.html:
• More than SR36 million ($5.6 million) in prizes will be awarded at the festival, organized by the National Center for Falcons

Updated 16 November 2026 22:16

November 16, 2026 22:16

RIYADH: The King Abdulaziz Falconry Festival will kick off on Tuesday in Malham, north of Riyadh, bringing together falconers from Saudi Arabia and abroad to compete in 140 rounds for prizes totaling more than SR36 million ($5.6 million).

Organized by the National Center for Falcons, the festival will run from Nov. 17 to 30 at the center’s headquarters, featuring competitions in the Milwah (lure flying) and Mazayen (falcon beauty) categories.

Cash prizes and titles will be at stake, including the King Abdulaziz Cups, Saif Al-Malik (the King’s Sword) and Shalfa Al-Malik.

National Center for Falcons spokesperson Waleed Al-Tawil said the festival reflects the Saudi leadership’s continued commitment to falconry, an ancient tradition and an integral part of Saudi identity.

He added that the center works to create a competitive environment that meets falconers’ needs and reflects the festival’s standing and the scale of local and international participation.

Last year’s event recorded the highest turnout in the festival’s history, with 3,536 falcons and 1,744 falconers from nine countries competing in 151 rounds. The festival has also set three Guinness World Records across its editions for the number of participating falcons.

This month’s Lifestyle Corner brings together a range of experiences across Saudi Arabia, from outdoor festivals and international sports in Riyadh to digital art in Diriyah, desert adventures in AlUla, and beach tennis in Jeddah. With festivals, cultural traditions, and seasonal entertainment also on the calendar, this November will offer residents and visitors plenty of ways to explore the Kingdom.

Riyadh: Major Events in the Capital


Riyadh Season

Riyadh Season returns with a ten-week program of sporting events, concerts, theatrical performances, and family entertainment. Announced attractions include Boulevard World, Boulevard City, Wonder Garden, The Groves, and the Farmers’ Market. Throughout November, visitors can explore different zones and choose from a broad calendar of activities across the capital.

Dates: Throughout November 2026; season opens October 21
Location: Various locations across Riyadh
Tickets and More Information: https://www.visitsaudi.com/en/seasons/riyadh-season

UCI Urban Cycling World Championships

Riyadh will host the UCI Urban Cycling World Championships for the second consecutive year, bringing together BMX Freestyle and trials competitions. From aerial tricks on ramps to displays of balance and precision, the championships offer spectators a chance to experience cycling disciplines that combine athletic skill with creativity.

Dates: November 3–7, 2026
Location: Riyadh
Tickets and More Information: https://www.uci.org/competition-details/2025/TRI/73824

KASHTA Festival

KASHTA brings Saudi outdoor culture into a three-day festival held within DUNES Expo. Planned activities include climbing, archery, camping gear experiences, survival skills workshops, and a dedicated children’s adventure zone. Food stalls and stage entertainment add to the program, making the festival an option for families and groups interested in outdoor recreation.

Dates: November 17–19, 2026
Location: Riyadh International Convention & Exhibition Center, Hall 4
Tickets, Registration, and More Information: https://kashtafestival.com/

PIF Saudi International Golf Tournament

The PIF Saudi International returns to Riyadh Golf Club as the final event of The International Series season. The tournament offers golfers and fans of the sport an opportunity to watch international professionals compete over four days. Its setting provides a different pace from the capital’s indoor shows and festivals, with spectators following the action around the course.

Dates: November 18–21, 2026
Location: Riyadh Golf Club
Tickets and More Information: https://www.uci.org/competition-details/2025/TRI/73824

King Abdulaziz Falconry Festival

For those interested in Saudi heritage, the King Abdulaziz Falconry Festival offers an opportunity to explore the longstanding tradition of falconry. The festival adds a cultural dimension to Riyadh’s November calendar, connecting visitors with a practice closely associated with the Kingdom’s history and identity.

Dates: November 17–30, 2026
Location: Riyadh
Tickets and More Information: https://www.visitsaudi.com/en/riyadh/events/king-abdulaziz-falconry-festival

Diriyah: CONTINUUM ’26

CONTINUUM ’26 presents work developed through Diriyah Art Futures’ Emerging New Media Artists Programme. The exhibition explores the meeting point of art and technology through immersive installations, moving image, sound, virtual reality, and other digital media. Visitors in early November can catch the final days of the exhibition before it closes on November 7.

Dates: Through November 7, 2026; opened September 3
Location: Diriyah Art Futures, Diriyah
Tickets and More Information: https://www.visitsaudi.com/en/diriyah/events/continuum-26-diriyah-art-futures

 
AlUla

AlUla Skies Festival

AlUla Skies Festival returns with experiences that invite visitors to discover the destination from above and beneath its night skies. The program includes sunrise hot air balloon journeys over Hegra, tethered balloon rides, illuminated balloon shows, and guided stargazing. With activities ranging from short ascents to evening experiences, the festival offers several ways to enjoy AlUla’s distinctive landscape.

Dates: November 6-15, 2026
Location: Various locations across AlUla
Tickets and More Information: https://www.experiencealula.com/en

Hegra Geology Hike

For visitors who prefer to explore on foot, the Hegra Geology Hike offers a guided introduction to the landscape of Saudi Arabia’s first UNESCO World Heritage Site. The limited-capacity experience focuses on rock formations and geological features, providing another way to appreciate Hegra beyond its celebrated monuments. The hike runs on Saturdays throughout November.

Dates: November 7, 14, 21, and 28, 2026
Location: Hegra, AlUla
Tickets and More Information: https://www.experiencealula.com/en/places-to-go/hegra

 
Jeddah

International Tennis Federation Beach Tennis Sand Series Tour Finals

Jeddah will host the International Tennis Federation (ITF) Beach Tennis Sand Series Tour Finals for the first time, bringing international competition to Al Ruwais Beach. The tournament will feature the top eight men’s and women’s doubles teams in the qualifying rankings and will be staged alongside the ITF Beach Tennis New Wave event. For residents and visitors along the Red Sea coast, it offers an opportunity to discover a different side of competitive tennis in a seaside setting.

Dates: November 26–December 5, 2026
Location: Al Ruwais Beach, Jeddah
Tickets and More Information: https://www.itftennis.com/en2026/

items.title: Phu Quoc, Vietnam
items.note: Asia's buzziest island hits peak season after a record-breaking tourism year.
items.read: Phu Quoc, voted Asia's best island by Condé Nast Traveler readers, earned $2.4B in tourism revenue in the first 10 months of the year, up 38%. Foreign arrivals jumped 59% to 2.14 million, and the island's November to April dry season is now underway.

article.html:
Phu Quoc, voted Asia's best island by Condé Nast Traveler readers, generated VND63 trillion (US$2.4 billion) in tourism revenue in the first 10 months of this year, up 38% year-on-year.

The Vietnam's largest island received 9.2 million tourist arrivals in the first 10 months, up 30% year-on-year, including 2.14 million foreign tourists, a 59% increase year-on-year and surpassing its full-year goal of 2 million.

In October alone, the island generated VND5.1 trillion in tourism revenues, up 37.8% year-on-year as foreign tourist arrivals surged 50% to 223,000, according to An Giang Province's Department of Tourism.

Tourists relax under the sun on a beach in Phu Quoc. Photo by Linh Huynh

The strong growth reflects Phu Quoc's growing appeal as a holiday destination, underpinned by investment in tourism infrastructure and a wider range of visitor experiences.

Improved air connectivity has also helped attract international visitors, with direct flights linking the island to key markets such as South Korea, Central Asia and Eastern Europe.

Phu Quoc's peak tourist season runs from November to April, coinciding with the island's dry season, which typically brings sunny weather, calm seas and low humidity.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI
items.note: After 16 years of waiting and two delays, GTA 6 launches tomorrow, Nov 19.
items.read: Grand Theft Auto 6 releases on November 19, 2026, billed as perhaps the most anticipated video game of all time. Several big publishers moved their games out of November to avoid competing with it.

article.html:
Published Nov 1, 2026, 12:01 AM EDT

Lee D’Amato is a writer born, raised, and based in Queens, New York. With collective thousands of hours in games like Final Fantasy, Metal Gear, Elden Ring, and The Legend of Zelda, he's now writes game features, guides, and reviews for Screen Rant, but has covered a wide range of topics, including ancient history, affordable travel, and overall health.

Sign in to your ScreenRant account

Multiple major video game releases are scheduled for November 2026 as the holiday season draws closer. At the top of almost everyone's list is Grand Theft Auto 6, perhaps the most anticipated video game release of all time, and projected to be so popular that the resulting productivity loss could have devastating effects on the US economy.

While multiple high-profile video game releases were delayed out of November to avoid the oncoming freight train of GTA 6, a few publishers, including fellow industry titan Nintendo, are brave enough to take it on. There are also a few dark horses coming out this month that you may want to keep an eye on.

GTA 6 Is The Biggest Release Of The Year

After 16 years of waiting, two delays, and endless leaks, rumors, and speculation, GTA 6 is finally coming out on November 19, 2026. This is, of course, the follow-up to Rockstar Games' record-breaking 2013 release Grand Theft Auto 5, although it follows a new cast of characters throughout an original story.

GTA 6 stars dual protagonists Lucia and Jason, residents of Vice City (the series' take on MIami, Florida). As they travel the open world, players can choose to keep the two together or split them up, engaging in all manner of crimes, misdemeanors, and side activities like scuba diving. GTA 6 will also employ a reputation system similar to Red Dead Redemption 2.

Of course, there's also the cars; players can steal or purchase a variety of different vehicles, with customization options available for most. Characters are also customizable, with a variety of clothing pieces and hairstyles to select from.

GTA 6 has already caused its fair share of controversy: some fans have raised concerns over its $80 price tag, the exclusive content included in its $100 premium edition, and its lack of a true physical (or PC) release at launch. But it's still expected to sell incredibly well, and, if it lives up to the hype and is truly the groundbreaking next-gen GTA we're all hoping it is, could be the game of the year for 2026.

Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Revives An All-Time Classic

One of few games willing to challenge GTA 6's dominance is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. Slated for release on November 5, this is a reimagining of the 1998 game of the same title, a highly influential release that introduced the world to 3D Zelda and can often be found high in the running on lists of the greatest games of all time.

The Ocarina of Time remake incorporates a new control scheme that includes full camera control, button-based jumping, and quick swapping between items. Link can now sprint instead of having to dodge roll everywhere, and there'll be a dedicated jump button instead of a finicky auto-jump system. Cutscenes are also fully voiced in the remake.

At the moment, it's not totally clear just how closely the Ocarina of Time remake will stick to the original version. We do know there are a couple of extras — Amiibo-exclusive in-game masks and the new Threads of Time quest tracking feature, for example — but beyond that, it's anyone's guess.

While some fans have questioned certain aspects of the remake (i.e., the new art style, the change in camera perspective, the need for a quest list, and the need for a remake in general), it's a new game in one of Nintendo's most popular franchises, so obviously, Ocarina of Time is going to be a big deal. It's the must-have Switch 2 game of the season.

World Of Warcraft: Forever Launches This Month

Coming out November 4 is World of Warcraft: Forever, a brand-new MMO set in the world of Azeroth. Conceived as a sort of alternate universe version of the original WoW, Forever will become a permanent, ever-expanding MMO, with regular updates and new content added periodically.

WoW: Forever already features a new race (Skyborn), three new zones, 1,000 new quests, nine new dungeons, a new battleground, two new raids, and lots of other content for players to explore. It's in early access at the moment, with a full launch slated for November 4.

Beyond the major releases, November 2026 is packed full of promising indie games and potential sleeper hits. Below is a list of every video game that comes out this month. items.title: Xiaomi 18 Pro & 18 Pro Max
items.note: Global launch with dual 200MP Leica cameras, a 0.99mm bezel and a rear display.
items.read: Xiaomi's new flagships went on sale globally on Nov 17. Both have a privacy display toggled by a new AI button, a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6, two 200MP cameras under flat glass, and a 4,000-nit rear OLED that can run apps like Google Maps and Spotify.

article.html:
Xiaomi is pushing the limits of modern smartphone specs with a killer design, flush camera lenses, and a next-gen Snapdragon SoC.

If you’re looking for a phone with top-tier specs, Xiaomi has a new phone for you. The Xiaomi 18 Pro and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max are the company’s latest flagships, available starting today, November 17. When looking at the spec list for the Xiaomi 18 series, it’s difficult to find anything that was left out.

During the launch presentation, Xiaomi emphasized that its new privacy display wasn’t just a copy of “other privacy displays.” Rather, they created an entirely new subpixel layout called HyperRGB 2.0 that delivers far higher resolution and brightness output than the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra. You can also enable and disable the privacy display feature on the Xiaomi 18 Pro series with a click of the new AI button on the left side of the phone. Functionally, Xiaomi’s privacy display looks nearly identical to Samsung’s, including the ability to have specific apps use it.

Both models feature identical specs, including the privacy display and cameras, with the exception of the screen size, battery capacity, and charging speed. Here are the differences:

The 120Hz LTPO display is bordered by a 0.99mm bezel, the smallest in the industry so far, 4,000-nit peak brightness, and TÜV Rheinland Triple Eye Care Certification, including a 2160Hz PWM dimming rate. Inside the phone is a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 processor with a 3D IceLoop cooling system, and each model’s silicon-carbon battery includes 28% silicon content.

On the back is a pair of 200MP cameras, including a 1/1.28-inch main sensor and a 1/1.56-inch periscope telephoto sensor. These are massive sensors, especially compared to the 1/3.94″ and 1/2.52″ telephoto sensors in the Galaxy S26 Ultra. Despite their size, Xiaomi packs them onto the back in an island with fully flat glass — no protruding camera lenses!

That island on the back isn’t just for cameras, though. It also packs in a 120Hz LTPO M11 OLED panel with 4,000-nit peak brightness for ultra-high-quality selfies and group shots, plus support for notifications and apps. Xiaomi created a new GenAI Apps feature that lets you create your own apps on the back display, plus official support for several popular apps like Google Maps, Spotify, and more.

The Xiaomi 18 Pro series ships with HyperOS 4 (Android 17) and includes 3 months of Google AI Pro, plus 5TB of Google Cloud storage. The Xiaomi 18 Pro retails for €1399 for the model with 12GB RAM and 256GB storage, or €1599 for 12GB/512GB. The Xiaomi 18 Pro Max starts at €1599 for 12GB/256GB, €1799 for 12GB/512GB, and a 16GB/1TB model will be available soon for €2099.

Some retailers also sell a bundle that includes the Official silicone magnetic case, which usually retails for €39, as well as the Magnetic Remote Stand, which retails for €69. That remote stand functions as a MagSafe-style stand and remote, giving you camera shutter functionality and a scrolling feature.

items.title: Island screen-time app
items.note: New YC-backed app turns staying off your phone into a farming game.
items.read: Island rewards you for meeting screen-time goals with a credit score that boosts your farm's production and unlocks crops and animals, a carrot-not-stick take on digital wellbeing. It came from founders Ashish Selvaraj and Ethan Pronev, as their fifth pivot at Y Combinator.

article.html:
A new startup is taking a different approach to helping people manage their screen time. Instead of blocking apps or restricting the phone’s use after a set period, an app called Island encourages you to meet your screen time goals by way of a farming simulator game. Yes, a game! Island works by rewarding you when you’re disciplined enough to meet your goals with a “credit score” that increases your farm’s production, unlocking new crops, animals, and other content.

This carrot-instead-of-stick approach was dreamed up by entrepreneurs Ashish Selvaraj (CEO) and Ethan Pronev (CTO), who met while studying at the University of Waterloo, then went on to work at companies that included Jane Street, Citadel Securities, Databricks, and Microsoft.

Later, they quit their jobs to join the startup accelerator Y Combinator, where they first tried out other ideas in areas like B2B and software-as-a-service, but weren’t finding the right fit.

Island ended up being their fifth pivot, and the first the founders actually found themselves enjoying.

“Once we were in YC, I think there’s a big mindset — I think in [San Francisco], in general — of, ‘selling shovels.’ Everyone wants to ‘sell shovels’ to other companies, and around us, that’s just what was going on,” explains Selvaraj, speaking about the concept that many successful startups sell the tools, infrastructure, or services to others following whatever the current market boom or trend may be.

“So all the ideas we had — we tried these things — but we found that we weren’t passionate about it. Like idea after idea seemed like ultimately the product was just a dashboard with some kind of different backend,” he added. “It felt like we quit our jobs … just to do something that was a variation of that.”

With Island, the team gets to tap into their creativity, having drawn the pixel art themselves.

“A lot of people do use [AI] models to generate the art, but we felt that it had a certain character when we drew it ourselves,” he told TechCrunch. “I feel like with Claude getting so good, there’s a tendency to give away every task to Claude. But ultimately it feels like there’s something else that comes out when you do it yourself, especially in something like art,” Selvaraj said.

What’s more, the app does appear to be successful in helping users meet their goals, the startup’s early data shows. After early testing and an October launch, the team says that the majority of its users (82%) will end their screen time right at the limit they’ve set. Many more are ending their screen time when they get the “15 minutes left” warning.

Island could appeal to those who have given up on other screen time apps out of frustration because the app doesn’t actually lock you out of apps or your phone. That’s something that can end up being more disruptive, especially when you’re in the middle of doing something, like posting, sharing, commenting, or chatting, among other things. Instead, Island taps into users’ own self-discipline and their desire to see their island flourish to encourage screen time breaks.

The idea to encourage users to keep their goals by offering some other type of in-app reward system isn’t entirely novel. Last year, Hank Green’s screen time app Focus Friend went viral for its experience, which involved a little friend that could only knit items that, in turn, allowed you to get points used to decorate your room when you were focused on your non-distracting apps.

Similar ideas have been used in self-care apps and habit-trackers like Finch, Amaru, Belly, Flora, Urso, and others. But Island expands this concept from being focused on helping out a virtual friend or pet to one that’s more of a game — and one where you can experience the consequences without “having to torture your pet,” notes Selvaraj.

Island also allows users to add friends and visit each other’s islands, compete in group challenges, and keep each other accountable by tying your island together with one friend of your choosing. In the latter scenario, if either friend goes over their limit, both of their islands will suffer.

The startup says Island has proven to be fairly “sticky” with a 51% daily active users-to-monthly active users ratio, and a day 30 retention rate of 49%, meaning 49% of users were still active on the app on the 30th day since the app was installed.

The app is currently free to use, with a $39.99 per year subscription that allows you to set individual limits on different apps, instead of just an overall daily screen time limit. The company hasn’t raised additional seed funding outside of YC, but plans to begin marketing the app on social media for the rest of the year.

items.title: 100 Days of Deception (K-drama)
items.note: Kim You Jung's spy romance reclaims No. 1 in Korea's drama buzz rankings.
items.read: tvN's 100 Days of Deception, a spy romance set in 1930s Gyeongseong, retook No. 1 on FUNdex's buzz rankings for Nov 9 to 15, beating Disney+'s The Remarried Empress. Star Kim You Jung also topped the cast ranking for the first time.

article.html:
by Hana, November 17, 2026 · Updated November 18, 2026

10

Kim You Jung of tvN's 100 Days of Deception has taken the top spot on Good Data Corporation's FUNdex drama cast buzz rankings for the first time since the show premiered, while the drama itself won back No. 1 among the most buzzworthy dramas, a week after losing it to Disney+'s The Remarried Empress.

FUNdex released its TV-OTT drama and cast buzz rankings for the second week of November (November 9 to 15) on November 17. FUNdex measures how much people are talking about TV and OTT shows and their cast, using news articles, blogs and online communities, videos and social media reactions. The previous week, The Remarried Empress had taken the top spot in its very first week.

The cast of 100 Days of Deception
Image via tvN

100 Days of Deception Reclaims No. 1

100 Days of Deception topped the chart for the third time in four weeks. It also led the combined drama and non-drama ranking with an 8.94% share, ahead of Netflix's new season of The Devil's Plan (6.93%) and The Remarried Empress (6.54%). Among dramas airing on TV only, it has now been No. 1 for four weeks in a row.

The spy romance set in 1930s Gyeongseong is also doing well in the ratings. Episodes 10 and 12, which aired on November 8 and 15, scored 10.7% and 10.4% nationwide (Nielsen Korea), the drama's second straight week in double digits.

Kim You Jung, who plays pickpocket-turned-spy Lee Ga Kyung, ranked No. 1 among drama cast members with a 3.82% share. Co-star Park Jin Young, who had been No. 1 for the previous two weeks, came in right behind her with 3.63%. Korean outlets noted that the cast top spot had gone to Kim Ji Won of Doctor X: Mafia in White or Park Jin Young every week since early October, until now.

Shin Min Ah and Lee Jong Suk in The Remarried Empress
Image via Disney+

The Remarried Empress slipped to second after its record-breaking debut week, and Doctor X: Mafia in White stayed in third. Two new dramas joined the top 10: SBS's Good Partner Season 2 entered at No. 9 before its premiere, and tvN's Happy Anding, which premiered on November 11, entered at No. 10.

1. 100 Days of Deception (tvN)

7. Yoo Yeon Seok, The Perfect Lie
8. Seol In Ah, Love in Disguise
9. Ju Ji Hoon, The Remarried Empress
10. Seo Hyun Jin, The Perfect Lie

items.title: Thalath Wahat
items.note: A quiet bookshop-cafe on Takhassusi, with Arabic and English shelves and a surprisingly good vanilla matcha.
items.read: Thalath Wahat, meaning "three oases," opened in August 2026 at Seven Square Mall on Al Takhassusi Street. This is Riyadh describes it as a bookshop, cafe and community space in one, with a large Arabic and English selection, tote-bag merch, and a November programme of talks, workshops, a reading club and children's activities. Arab News found it notably quiet on weekday visits and laptop-friendly, and singled out the vanilla matcha with coconut milk; the honey cake was creamy, if milder than expected.
facts: Arabic and English books, vanilla matcha
Two basement levels at the mall (Arab News)
items.mapQuery: Thalath Wahat Seven Square Mall Al Takhassusi Riyadh

article.html:
Book lovers, you’ll want to add Thalath Wahat to your Riyadh list! It’s a bookshop, café and community space all in one, and a lovely spot to spend a few hours away from the crowded coffee shop scene.

First, the design is beautiful! The space has a calm and cosy feel, making it a great place to read, work or study. There’s also a huge selection of books in both Arabic and English, so you’ll have plenty to browse. And if you love bookish accessories, check out their merchandise. They have some really nice tote bags to carry your books around!

Of course, you can also grab a coffee, matcha, herbal tea or something sweet from the café while you read or get some work done.

Bringing the kids? They’ll enjoy it too! Thalath has children’s books and activities that help little ones discover the fun of reading. They will get to spend more time around books.

There’s always something happening here, too. The November cultural programme includes three dialogue and intellectual sessions, workshops, a reading club, and activities for children.

If you’re looking for a quiet place to get some work done or a reading spot, Thalath is worth a visit!

Location: Al Takhassusi

items.title: Dips Plus, Diriyah
items.note: A Najdi-style courtyard cafe just off the Diriyah tourist trail, quietly serving refined cakes and hanini baklava.
items.read: LIST came across Dips Plus by accident in historic Diriyah, tucked away from Bujairi Terrace and Al Samhaniya Street, less than a kilometre from JAX. The two-floor space is designed around batn al-huwi, a traditional Najdi courtyard, with an upstairs terrace looking toward Wadi Hanifa. Standout bites were honey cake, Matilda cake, and baklava filled with hanini, from a kitchen overseen by Saudi chef Salman Al-Ateeq. The official site says it is open 24 hours, with no booking needed, at Prince Abdullah Bin Abdelrahman in Al Diriyah Al Jadidah.
facts: Honey cake, Matilda cake, hanini baklava
items.mapQuery: Dips Plus Prince Abdullah Bin Abdelrahman Al Diriyah Al Jadidah

article.html:
There is a saying that chance can outdo even the best-laid plans. A recent visit to Dips Plus Café and Restaurant proved exactly that.

What began as an accidental discovery quickly eclipsed experiences at Michelin-starred restaurants. In historic Diriyah district, beyond the polished Bujairi Terrace and away from the casual gatherings along Al Samhaniya Street, the cafe reveals itself quietly. Tucked into a corner just under a kilometre from JAX District, it is the kind of place you’re unlikely to find unless you’re not looking for it at all. And yet, in that moment of misdirection, we stumbled upon what can only be described as one of Diriyah’s best-kept secrets.

Do not judge it by its exterior

Dips Plus Cafe Diriyah 8

Dips Plus Cafe Diriyah 9

At first glance, Dips Plus resists easy categorisation. It appears to be a cafe, but the experience extends well beyond that label. The “Made in Diriyah” phrase etched onto a wall hints at something more deliberate, more rooted. The space unfolds across two floors. Downstairs, indoor seating is spacious and quietly comfortable, offering a sense of privacy rarely found in cafes. At its centre, an outdoor courtyard, framed by soft lighting, trees, and a swing, feels closer to a private home than a commercial venue.

By chance, we met Osama bin Mohammed, one of the executives behind Dips Plus, who described the design as inspired by batn al-huwi, a traditional Najdi architectural concept. In this style, the main living space opens to the sky, overlooked by the upper floor, with arches and heritage details shaping the interior. Gravel flooring completes the effect, evoking the courtyards of old Najdi homes.

Dips Plus Cafe Diriyah 7

Dips Plus Cafe Diriyah 11

Lead Hidden Gem Dips Plus 1

Upstairs, the atmosphere shifts. Outdoor seating opens onto views of Wadi Hanifa, a rare vantage point shared only with a handful of locations in Diriyah. In spring, the evening breeze carries a welcome softness. Come winter, fire pits warm the tables. Even in summer, the setting remains inviting, aided by Diriyah’s comparatively milder climate and discreet misting systems that make year-round outdoor dining possible.

A series of pleasant surprises

Dips Plus Cafe Diriyah 4

Dips Plus Cafe Diriyah 6

Dining always comes with expectations. At Michelin-starred restaurants or five-star hotels, those expectations are naturally high. At more modest venues, they tend to be tempered. Here, however, the experience quietly defies those assumptions.

It began with honey cake, unexpectedly refined, delivering a true depth of flavour. Then came the slice of Matilda Cake, equally assured. But it was the final pairing, the coffee of the day served alongside baklava filled with hanini, that shifted the experience into something more memorable.

Cafes often rely on external kitchens, with predictable results. But this was different. Turkish baklava reimagined with a traditional Saudi Najdi filling is not a casual menu addition. It suggests a chef with both confidence and clarity of vision, merging two culinary traditions into a single, cohesive dish.

Dips Plus Cafe Diriyah 13

Dips Plus Cafe Diriyah 5

The story behind Dips Plus

Dips Plus Cafe Diriyah 2

Dips Plus Cafe Diriyah 3

That vision belongs to Saudi chef, Salman Al-Ateeq, the driving force behind Dips Plus. With more than 35 years of experience in luxury hospitality, his presence is quietly felt rather than publicly advertised. Unlike many contemporary chefs, he maintains little to no visibility on social media or search platforms.

His background spans high-end hotels and the launch of multiple restaurant and cafe concepts across Saudi Arabia. Today, through Dips Plus, he oversees a menu that moves seamlessly between local and international dishes. The kitchen’s reach extends beyond the cafe itself, supplying food across Riyadh through delivery platforms and catering to hotel buffets throughout the city.

Dips Plus is understated in its approach, letting the experience speak for itself. Its strength lies in what it delivers quietly: a strong sense of place, a thoughtful reinterpretation of tradition, and the kind of culinary precision more often associated with far grander settings.

items.title: With Heart, Lift Studio
items.note: A small matcha bar hidden inside an art studio in JAX, with flavours you will not see on every Riyadh menu.
items.read: This is Riyadh's May 2026 guide found With Heart tucked inside Lift Studio in JAX, so a matcha sits among sketchbooks, workshops and people painting. The menu leans into unusual flavours such as Birthday Cake, Coconut Cloud, Lavender, Earl Grey and Miso Caramel matcha; coffee drinkers can order a Latte Cloud or Honey Espresso instead. Wanderlog lists the host studio, Lift Studio/Space/Gallery, at 4.6 from 162 reviews, and notes it is easy to miss, behind a Starbucks Reserve, in Al Mathar Ash Shmali.
facts: Al Mathar Ash Shmali, Riyadh 13732 (Lift Studio, per Wanderlog)

article.html:
Matcha lovers, this one is for you. Hidden inside an art studio in Riyadh’s JAX District, With Heart is serving some of the best matcha in the city!

At first, it looks like a small specialty matcha bar. But once you walk in, you realize the experience is much bigger than that. The café is tucked inside Lift Studio, so the whole space is surrounded by art, workshops, sketchbooks, paintings, and people creating around you. Instead of the usual loud café atmosphere, everything feels calm, creative, and personal.

And of course, the drinks are a big part of why people keep coming back. Their menu is full of unique matcha flavors that feel fun and unusual. The Birthday Cake Matcha is sweet, creamy, and tastes like dessert in a cup. The Coconut Cloud Matcha is lighter and refreshing, while the Lavender Matcha has a soft, floral flavor that somehow complements the earthy taste of matcha.

If you like trying unusual combinations, the Earl Grey Matcha and Miso Caramel Matcha are worth ordering. The miso caramel one especially stands out with its mix of sweet and slightly salty flavors that you probably won’t find anywhere else in Riyadh.

Not a matcha person? They also serve coffee drinks like the Latte Cloud and Honey Espresso, so nobody feels left out.

But what really makes this place special is the atmosphere. You could be sipping an iced matcha while an art workshop is happening right next to you. You will see people painting, friends catching up, and someone else quietly working in the corner.

So if you’re looking for somewhere different from the usual coffee run, this hidden matcha bar in Riyadh might end up becoming your new favorite place.

If you like trying unusual combinations, the Earl Grey Matcha and Miso Caramel Matcha are worth ordering. The miso caramel one especially stands out with its mix of sweet and slightly salty flavors that you probably won’t find anywhere else in Riyadh. Not a matcha person? They also serve coffee drinks like the Latte Cloud and Honey Espresso, so nobody feels left out.

But what really makes this place special is the atmosphere. You could be sipping an iced matcha while an art workshop is happening right next to you. You will see people painting, friends catching up, and someone else quietly working in the corner.
So if you’re looking for somewhere different from the usual coffee run, this hidden matcha bar in Riyadh might end up becoming your new favorite place.

article.html:
Riyadh’s coffee scene has entered a new phase, with fresh brands launching by the dozen and long-standing cafes from Jeddah, Al Khobar and beyond setting their sights on the capital. Here, in a nation where the average citizen downs more than 600 cups of coffee a year, old-school tea houses stand shoulder-to-shoulder with a new breed of homegrown heroes – tucked into backstreets, repurposed warehouses and unlikely pockets of greenery – while global giants jostle for attention, eager to carve out their own niche in the city’s fast-maturing caffeine scene. These are the best cafes in Riyadh to sip and soak it all in.

Ba'a Bakehouse

Reached via a dusty, unassuming road through an otherwise unremarkable neighbourhood, this ultra-soulful cafe sits on Riyadh’s far western flank, perched above the green ribbon of Wadi Hanifah and feeling pleasingly removed from the city’s sprawl. Although the pale, plant-flecked interiors alone justify the journey – there's always competition for the much-coveted sofa, but plenty of tables spill across the space along with an outdoor terrace beneath twinkling trees – but the real rewards are edible: fudgy brownies layered with cheesecake, simple grilled cheese sandwiches, fresh fruit danishes and bites of rocky road that disappear far too quickly. Don’t be deterred by the queue at the door — much of it is takeaway traffic, and moves fast.

Address: Al Rafiah, Riyadh

Arwana Artisan Bakehouse

You could easily spend an afternoon picking through Arwana’s bread platter alone: warm, freshly baked loaves torn apart and dragged through cool, tangy labneh, clouds of whipped feta and an addictive sun-dried tomato spread — all outrageously good value at SAR37 ($9.85). But that would mean missing the rest of the menu, from Bombay-style eggs with real heat to deeply spiced shakshoukas, pillowy omelettes and some of the best Montreal-style bagels in Riyadh, fat and chewy, stuffed with dill-flecked cream cheese and slivers of smoked salmon. More than a dozen different breads are baked on site each day and sold to take away, including crusty sourdough country loaves, glossy brioche baguettes, pain du Maroc, soft split rolls and pillowy shokupan — although nothing quite compares to tasting it fresh from the oven.

Address: 2701 King Abdullah Branch Road, King Salman Neighbourhood, Riyadh

Urth Caffé

Packed with organic options for vegans and the health-conscious (including surprisingly excellent plant-based chocolate cake), this bohemian cafe from California focuses on all-natural dishes free from artificial ingredients or refined sugars. Homely bread pudding breakfast bowls, hearty portions of lasagna and scrambles with eggs from vegetarian-fed chickens keep diners coming back, but it’s the commitment to coffee and tea that truly sets Urth apart. It all started in 1989 when Jilla and Shallom Berkman met a farmer from Peru who introduced them to rare heirloom coffee trees. Fast forward to 2017, and Urth Caffé opened its Riyadh branch, continuing the tradition of serving exceptional, earth-friendly dishes and drinks. The Manhattan Mudd, a smooth and complex African-Asian blend straight from New York, pairs perfectly with a slice of old-fashioned Granny Smith apple pie, baked fresh daily using classic recipes.

Address: Prince Muhammad Ibn Abd Al Aziz, As Sulimaniyah, Riyadh

On

Ar Rawdah is packed with cafes, but bistro-style On is one of the neighbourhood’s loveliest and most eclectic places to spend an afternoon, with plenty of tucked-away nooks for reading, studying or people-watching. The bargain breakfast platter is a highlight – doughy flatbreads hot from the kitchen, labneh drizzled with olive oil, eggs, za'atar and small bowls of spreads – best enjoyed with a steaming pot of tea.

Address: Ibn Khaldun Street, Ar Rawdah, Riyadh

OffBrief

Since opening late last year, OffBrief has quickly claimed its place as the gravitational centre of Riyadh’s Jax District – an enclave of warehouses and concrete courtyards reborn as the city’s creative quarter – drawing a fashion-first crowd with its glowing red counters and restless creative energy that never quite settles. Crowd-pulling signatures include crème brûlée lattes with crackable caramelised sugar crusts, buttery banana bread served fresh from the oven and wintery hot chocolates crowned with clouds of whipped cream.

Address: Jax District, Diriyah, Riyadh

Tomoor AlUla

Dates are as central to Saudi life as coffee, and Tomoor AlUla brings the two together in a cosy cafe space that subtly evokes the ancient dunes of Hegra in the Kingdom’s northwest. The menu centres on pristine Safawy, Saggai and Monefi dates — served plain, stuffed or paired with chocolate — designed to be enjoyed alongside Saudi coffee in the way tradition intended: slowly, generously and in good company. While Tomoor has several branches across Riyadh, the standout is its outpost inside Smaa Gallery, a design-led complex of pale stone, soaring atriums and gallery-like calm packed with local boutiques and coffee shops.

Address: Prince Turki Bin Abdulaziz Al Awal Road, Al Malqa, Riyadh

Batla

A few minutes’ drive from Ba’a Bakehouse, Batla carries a similarly leafy, sun-drenched aesthetic, albeit without the crowds and long queues. Parquet floors, soft green accents and clusters of plants frame low tables and sink-in sofas, creating a space that feels far more like a well-styled living room than a city coffee stop — complete with thick hot chocolates, free lemon-infused water (still a rarity in Riyadh) and delicately illustrated cups tailor-made for Instagram.

Address: Prince Talal, Al Uraija, Riyadh

Bohemia Records & Cafe

Independent record store Bohemia began life in Al Khobar before hauling its 1,000-strong vinyl library west to Jax District’s The Warehouse, a homegrown cultural haunt that fills fast on weekends when live sets and Taylor Swift nights ricochet across the concrete floors. Wooden box shelves crammed with records – well-thumbed classics, new releases, the odd collector’s gem – wrap around a handful of neon-lit tables, where regulars linger over lattes and sweet treats served from the counter.

Address: Jax District, Diriyah, Riyadh

Brew92

Don’t expect “one coffee, please” to cut it here — the Brew92 team are serious about their beans. Trained to the Specialty Coffee Association’s exacting standards, they make regular visits to farms around the world to find the best flavours and strictly brew at 92°C in a bid to extract the optimum flavour profile from each roast. You’ll find all the classics on the menu (plus plenty of alternative milks for vegans), but the most interesting options are in the “stranger drinks” section — ice cream sandwiches dunked in espresso, cold pistachio lattes and crème-brulée brews.

Address: Uthman Ibn Affan Road, An Narjis, Riyadh

Elixir Bunn Coffee Roasters

Terracotta-coloured arches inspired by traditional Islamic architecture frame sleek, honey-hued tables at this oasis of calm — a minimalist “deco temple” of Saudi coffee once lauded by Architectural Digest Middle East for its unique design. Elixir Bunn, brewing beans since 2014, serves up blends inspired by the distinct aromas of the Kingdom’s regions. The Western version bursts with the warmth of cardamom, cloves, saffron and mastic, while the light-roasted Southern blend delivers a subtly sweet profile with ginger, fennel and cinnamon. Pair your coffee with a dense slice of chocolate-flecked banana bread or seasonal sweets like Kohei-Ziri, a Japanese dessert marrying the sweetness of vanilla ice cream with the bitterness of espresso.

Address: 7157 Salem Bin Maaqil, Al Nakheel

items.read: Backpacks, made by Aman Jaiswal, is a free iPhone app for saving and later finding links, screenshots, files and notes. You add links from the share sheet; text inside screenshots is read on the device, and the library syncs through your own iCloud, with no account required. Version 2.2 is on the App Store and needs iOS 26 or later. An optional assistant called Buddy stays off until you turn it on; the app has no reader view or offline reading, so it is a saver, not a full Instapaper replacement.

article.html:
Shotbolt: Everything you want in one screenshot app

from changing the words inside a screenshot to automatic redaction, recording and step guides.

Launch price until December 31, 2026, then $19.99.Free forever. Every download starts with 7 days of Pro. Requires macOS 26 or later.

One shortcut for every kind of capture.

Press it, then drag an area, snap to an element or choose another capture.

  1. The screen freezes. The magnifier shows each pixel, so you start on the exact one.

  2. One element. Press E, and one click selects the photo under the pointer, edges and all.Element capture is Pro (Shotbolt Pro).

  3. One bar makes a picture, text, a table, a long page, a video or a GIF.Each letter is a key. Table, Scroll, Record and GIF are Pro (Shotbolt Pro).

  4. Copied and saved. The card keeps it close to mark up, pin or drag into an app.

Edit any mark after you save.

Each arrow, note and cover is its own layer, so one moves without the rest.

  1. Point it out. Marks pin down the wrong total, and each one becomes a row in Layers.

  2. Hide a layer. The eye on its row in Layers hides that mark and leaves the rest.

  3. Fix the words. Edit Text changes €314 to €304 in the original's size, color and weight.

    Edit Text is Pro (Shotbolt Pro).

  4. Keep it private. Cover the email address by hand, or let Redact find the card number.

    Redact is Pro (Shotbolt Pro).

Search the words in your screenshots.

Type a word you remember, and the screenshot that shows it turns up.

  1. Any word. The search field takes a place, a price or part of an error.

  2. Names first. Captures with the word in their name sit on top, under Name matches.

  3. Found in text. Then come screenshots that hold the word, each with the line it is in.

  4. Sorted for you. Each screenshot gets a category, such as Receipt, and a title you can read.

Every click becomes a numbered step.

Start Steps and book the stay: each click lands in the guide, titled.

  1. Start Steps. Pick Steps on the All-In-One bar, or Record Step Guide in the menu.

    Step guides are Pro (Shotbolt Pro).

  2. Just click. Each click is a step: its screenshot, a marker where you clicked, a number.

  3. Titled for you. Each step is named after what you clicked, like Click 'Ribeira loft' in Safari.

  4. Share it. Export the guide as a PDF, one image, a GIF, HTML or Markdown.

Share any capture as a .

One key puts the link on your clipboard, with a password by default.

Everything you expect, and then some.

Six more things Shotbolt made today. Pro is marked; everything else is free.

Free

Every kind of screenshot, the editor with layers, text capture, pins and History with search. No time limit.

Pro

Edit Text, Element capture, Redact, step guides, recording and GIF, scrolling capture and every other tool marked Pro (Shotbolt Pro). One payment.

Your captures stay on your Mac.

Shotbolt reads the words in your screenshots so you can find one later.

  1. On your Mac. Apple’s text recognition does the reading, so no screenshot goes to a server.

  2. Yours to switch. On a Mac with Apple Intelligence, one switch turns off everything that uses it.

    Search works on every Mac, with the switch on or off.

  3. Yours to share. Shotbolt uploads a capture only for a share link you make. No account needed.

Shotbolt also goes online for a daily update check you can turn off, a license check with a Pro key and product news you sign up for. None of them sends a capture.

We built the screenshot app we wanted.

WindowServer

Apple · Part of macOS · PID 401

Part of macOS

Signed by Apple. This is a genuine part of macOS.

What is it?

Draws every window, menu and animation you see on screen, and routes your clicks and keystrokes.

Why it gets busy
  • Many open windows, or apps that redraw constantly (animated web pages, video, games)
  • Several or high-resolution external displays, especially at scaled resolutions
  • Transparency and motion effects, Stage Manager, or many desktops with live content
What you can do
  • Close windows and browser tabs you don't need, especially ones playing video or animation
  • Quit apps one at a time and watch whether WindowServer drops, to find the trigger
  • Turn on Reduce transparency and Reduce motion in System Settings > Accessibility > Display

Force quitting WindowServer instantly logs you out and closes all your apps, so unsaved work is lost.

items.title: Espanso
items.note: A free, open-source text expander for Windows, macOS and Linux that turns short triggers into snippets, dates or script output.
items.read: Espanso is a privacy-first, cross-platform text expander: type a short keyword and it replaces it as you go, in most apps. It can insert dates and emoji, run shell commands or scripts, use forms for reusable templates, and add community packages from the Espanso Hub. Configuration is file-based, there is a search bar (Alt+Space), and it is free under the GPL-3 license on Windows, macOS and Linux.

article.html:
Tired of typing the same sentences over and over?
Discover the incredible power of a full-blown text expander.

How it works

Espanso detects when you type a keyword

and replaces it while you're typing.

What people say about Espanso

I'd like to give a shout out to @terzi_federico for creating Espanso: https://espanso.org, an Open Source text expander.

Gotta love tools like these. I've just installed it and already know that it'll save me hours and hours! :)

Sébastien Dubois

Author, Crafter for 15+y, CTO, Indie Hacker

One of my favourite free productivity tools is espanso https://espanso.org It's a text expander. I mostly use it to write out quick text snippets such as:

My current IP, Today's date, Generic XSS payloads, Code snippets, Email templates

It's so good!

Luke Stephens

Founder @haksecio

Discovered https://espanso.org today. Fantastic tool for snippet expansion: Cross Platform and Open Source. Converted 50% of my TextExpander snippets so far. Still many to go. Will it become my goto? I don't know ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ Trial commences!

Rheinard Korf

Software Architect/Engineer

I have been using @terzi_federico's espanso for replacing text with emojis (e.g., :cowboy hat face: => 🤠), and it's fantastic. As a text expander, it can do a lot more than just that. Check it out!

Kevin Swiber

Smarter typing

No more copy and pasting, create

templates once and let Espanso do the rest for you.

Customer support replies, sales pitches, medical reports, you name it. Espanso got you covered.

Every sentence, one search away

Don’t remember a shortcut? No worries.

Just press

ALT+Space

and Espanso’s search bar

will open, letting you search for the perfect snippet.

Dates, Emojis 🚀, and more...

Don’t wrap your head around

dates. Espanso makes it easy to use them, both past and future ones.

Bring emojis 🤠 in all your favorite apps, one shortcut away.

Endless extensibility

Extend Espanso’s capabilities with

packages, or create your owns and share them with the community on the

Espanso Hub.

Need to insert mathematical notation? Or perhaps german accents? We got a package for them.

We even got the shrug ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

Advanced features

Shell and Script support

For advanced use-cases, you can extend Espanso’s snippets with

shell commands or

custom scripts.

No more copy-pasting from the terminal, inject the output into applications directly.

Form support

Use forms to handle complex workflows, creating templates that can be reused with ease.

You can even forward form values into custom scripts, opening up endless possibilities.

And also

System-wide integration

Espanso works with most applications, so you can boost your productivity everywhere.

File-based configuration

Espanso follows a Unix-like configuration philosophy, using simple files. Though a GUI is planned in the future.

Open-source license

Espanso is open-source, licensed under the GPL-3 license.

Cross-platform support

Espanso supports Windows, Linux and macOS.

Donate

Hi! I'm Federico, the creator of espanso. If you liked the project, please consider making a small donation, it really helps :)

Also, if you are looking to create educational videos such as tutorials, courses, and product demos, you might enjoy my latest project, Borumi.

A special thanks goes to all the wonderful people who supported espanso along the way

Together, we will make espanso the first universal text expander, open to everyone.
